assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, proglucagon processing, insulinotropic activity of GLP-1(7-36)) led to incretin therapies that have transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. A clear discovery chain from basic physiology to a large, durable change in medicine and in the research field.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 biology and secretion), Drucker (physiology, GLP-2, mechanism of action) and Mojsov (identification of the active peptide form) are the most defensible trio from the credited names; Knudsen's contribution is mainly drug development and Habener is not on the list. Mojsov's credit relative to others is historically contested.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, multiple approved drugs and large outcome trials; recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit for identifying active GLP-1 is disputed and I cannot verify the details independently.
Whether a prize would fold in the drug-development side (Knudsen) or stay with physiology is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a general method for causal control of defined cell populations with light; it changed experimental practice across fields and has begun clinical translation (vision restoration).
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and its deployment in neurons (Deisseroth, Boyden) are intertwined; six credited names exceed the three-laureate limit, so Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck would be left out despite strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Method widely replicated for over a decade, with extensive independent confirmation; ready for recognition.
uncertainties: Credit among Boyden, Deisseroth, Bamberg, Nagel, Hegemann and Miesenböck is contested and cannot be cleanly resolved.
Clinical impact is still early compared with research impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR identifies a central nutrient- and growth-signalling kinase controlling cell growth and metabolism, with consequences for cancer, immunosuppression, ageing and metabolic disease. Highly original and conceptually foundational.
assessment.attribution: Schreiber (rapamycin target chemistry, FKBP12-rapamycin) and Hall (genetic discovery of TOR in yeast) are the core contributors; Sabatini's later mTOR work is important but I would avoid it for a leaner configuration, and credit among the mammalian-TOR cloners is a complication.
assessment.maturity: Over thirty years of confirmation; drugs (rapalogs) are in clinical use; interpretation stable and still expanding.
uncertainties: Whether Hall alone or with Schreiber best captures the decisive discovery is unresolved.
Mammalian TOR identification involved several groups whose credit I cannot verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signalling logic from ER to nucleus (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing), explaining proteostasis, secretory-cell function and disease mechanisms.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter are the clear decisive pair, with the IRE1 and transcriptional-response discoveries; the two-person credited list gives a clean and fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature (1990s discoveries, extensive confirmation, conserved from yeast to mammals). Disease-therapeutic translation is less advanced.
uncertainties: Contributions of other groups (e.g. Ron, Kaufman) are not on the list and may be seen as relevant.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING reveals how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, linking infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer immunology; a clear mechanistic discovery with broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAMP and cGAS discovery) is decisive; STING identification credits Ishikawa and Barber. Sun and Wu were in Chen's group and their role is part of the same discovery, so a Chen-led trio is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Core mechanism confirmed independently across many labs since 2008-2013; therapeutic applications are still emerging, so somewhat younger than other candidates.
uncertainties: Clinical validation of STING agonists and inhibitors is limited so far.
Division of credit between STING discoverers and cGAS discoverers is a judgement call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 established the control of apoptosis as a cancer mechanism (cell survival rather than proliferation) and led to venetoclax, a targeted therapy; a conceptually important and clinically validated finding.
assessment.attribution: Adams and Cory (cloning, BCL-2 family biology) with Vaux (BCL-2 as survival gene) are the core; Strasser is also strong, and Korsmeyer and Tsujimoto are not on the list but historically relevant. Four credited names exceed three places.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation and approved therapy; timely.
uncertainties: Historical credit involving Tsujimoto, Korsmeyer and others outside the supplied list is not captured.
Overlap with earlier apoptosis prize (C. elegans) may affect perceived novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells created a new class of living drug with durable remissions in B-cell malignancies; major clinical and conceptual impact on cancer immunotherapy.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain developed the clinically effective CAR designs and Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy; Zelig Eshhar and others not credited here are relevant, so the supplied configuration is arguably incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and multiyear follow-up; safety, solid-tumour limits and cost remain, but the core success is established.
uncertainties: Missing foundational credit (e.g. Eshhar) cannot be resolved from the supplied names.
Long-term durability and generalisation beyond haematological cancers are not yet settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Wnt (Int-1/Wingless) unified cancer genes and developmental signalling, defining a major pathway in cell fate, stem-cell maintenance and tumorigenesis; foundational for developmental biology and cancer biology.
assessment.attribution: Nusse and Varmus discovered Int-1 as a mouse mammary oncogene and Nusse linked it to Wingless; Varmus has already been a laureate, so the allocation could weigh toward Nusse; the supplied pair is a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of confirmation across species; therapeutic translation is limited so far.
uncertainties: Competing credit for the Drosophila wingless genetics and the Wnt receptor/pathway (e.g. Frizzled, beta-catenin work) is outside the list.
Varmus's prior prize may weigh against.
